channel.title: Dottra blog
channel.description: Practical guides on money, mobile money and credit in Zambia.

item.title: What to check before you use a borrowing app in Zambia
item.description: Questions to ask before you sign up, the warning signs of a bad lender, and where to complain if something goes wrong.

item.title: Managing money as a government-sponsored student in Zambia
item.description: How to plan around allowance payments, cover the gaps when they're late, and avoid ending the semester in debt.

item.title: Salary advance or credit facility? How to choose when payday is too far away
item.description: How a salary advance from your employer compares with a reusable credit facility on cost, speed, privacy and what you can use it for.

item.title: Mobile money in Zambia: MTN MoMo, Airtel Money and Zamtel compared
item.description: How mobile money wallets work in Zambia, what to check on fees and limits, and how to keep your wallet and PIN safe.

item.title: How the Dottra credit facility works, from your first draw to your first statement
item.description: What happens when you draw, how the processing fee and monthly charge are worked out, and what a monthly statement shows.

item.title: How to get out of debt when you owe more than one person
item.description: List everything you owe, protect the essentials, choose an order to pay things off, and stop new borrowing from undoing the progress.

item.title: A monthly budget you can actually keep on a Zambian salary
item.description: Start from your net pay, take out what can't move, and give everything else a job before payday instead of after.

item.title: Planning for the costs that come once a year in Zambia
item.description: School terms, January uniforms, road tax, December. How to turn the big yearly costs into a small monthly amount so they stop arriving as emergencies.

item.title: How to build an emergency fund when your salary barely covers the month
item.description: Where to keep it, how much to aim for first, and how to start when there's nothing left over at the end of the month.

item.title: How to use a credit facility without falling behind
item.description: A credit limit is not money you have. Four habits that keep a reusable facility useful instead of becoming a balance you carry every month.
